items.question: What wondrous behavior may arise in a Kaula person through devotional absorption?
premises: Devotional absorption can manifest in Kaula practitioners
Such manifestations may appear wondrous or extraordinary
items.inference: Whatever wondrous behavior arises in a Kaula person comes from absorption in devotion.
items.plain_english: Whatever wondrous behavior appears in a Kaula person arises from absorption in devotion.

items.question: Why are those whose minds are attached to the deity considered always pure?
premises: Some practitioners have minds attached to the deity
The goddess herself is pure
Divine attachment confers purity
items.inference: Those whose minds are attached to the deity are always pure, for the goddess is indeed pure.
items.plain_english: Those whose minds are attached to the deity are always pure, for the goddess is indeed pure.

items.question: To whom do the pure devotees transmit the mantras they receive?
premises: Pure devotees receive or know mantras
Kaulas are fit recipients within this context
Transmission occurs through declaration
items.inference: Those pure devotees declare their mantras to the Kaulas.
uncertainties: Whether 'te' refers to the devotees or to divine agents is context-dependent
items.plain_english: They declare those mantras to the Kaulas.

items.question: How might participants behave when agitated by intoxication within the ritual circle?
premises: The ritual circle involves intoxicating substances
Intoxication can agitate participants
Agitation may produce laughter or anger
items.inference: In the circle, those agitated by honey-intoxication may laugh or may become angry.
items.plain_english: In the circle, those agitated by the intoxication of honey may laugh or become angry.

items.question: What conduct is required toward those acting erratically in the ritual circle?
premises: Participants may behave unpredictably in the circle
Ritual conduct must avoid causing harm
Proper practice is enjoined
items.inference: One should do no harm and should act with proper conduct.
uncertainties: Implicit object of conduct may be the intoxicated participants
items.plain_english: One should do no harm and should act properly.

items.question: How should one mentally regard those who are agitated by intoxication?
premises: Intoxicated participants may appear disturbed
Ritual vision transforms perception
They should be seen as divine
items.inference: Seeing those agitated by intoxication, one should regard them with the awareness that they are deities.
items.plain_english: Seeing those agitated by intoxication, one should regard them with the awareness of deity.

items.question: What ritual status do all social classes attain within the Bhairavi circle?
premises: The Bhairavi circle is a ritual context
Social classes exist outside the circle
Ritual participation confers elevated status
items.inference: In the Bhairavi circle, all social classes are twice-born.
items.plain_english: In the circle of Bhairavi, all social classes are twice-born.

items.question: From what source does the greatness of participants in the circle arise?
premises: Participants gain a special status
The goddess's worship is the central ritual use
Ritual application confers greatness
items.inference: Their greatness arises from their application in the worship of the goddess.
uncertainties: Subject is implicit from previous verse
items.plain_english: This greatness comes from their use in the worship of the goddess.

items.question: What equality among participants is affirmed within the middle of the ritual circle?
premises: The ritual circle suspends ordinary distinctions
Participants are ritually transformed
Tradition declares their divine equality
items.inference: In the middle of the circle there is no difference; all are remembered as equal to gods.
items.plain_english: In the middle of the circle there is no difference; all are regarded as equal to the gods.

items.question: Why must no distinction be made among the women present in the ritual circle?
premises: All women in the circle are identified as Pārvatīs
Divine identity removes ordinary distinctions
Making distinctions contradicts this identity
items.inference: Since all are Pārvatīs, one should not make any distinction.
items.plain_english: And all are Pārvatīs; therefore one should make no distinction.

items.question: What sacred substance is identified with Mahāmāyā in this ritual context?
premises: Mahāmāyā is invoked in the rite
A specific nectar is ritually central
The nectar is linked to the goddess's yoni
items.inference: Mahāmāyā is present as the nectar of the goddess's vulva.
uncertainties: Syntactic connection to following verse is implied
items.plain_english: Mahāmāyā is the nectar of the goddess's vulva.

items.question: Under what condition may one ritually approach a woman in this practice?
premises: Approach to a woman is ritually regulated
Consecration purifies the act
The practice is prescribed by injunction
items.inference: Because it is prescribed, one should approach a woman who has been purified by consecration.
items.plain_english: Because it is prescribed, one should approach a woman purified by consecration.

items.question: What benefits are said to result from performing this rite ten times?
premises: The rite yields specific fruits
Repetition increases efficacy
Ten performances are specified
items.inference: By ten times, one obtains a son and becomes free from disease.
uncertainties: Exact referent of 'daśabhiḥ' (ten times or ten days) is unclear
items.plain_english: By doing it ten times, one gains a son and becomes free from disease.

items.question: What supreme worldly attainment is promised within a year of this practice?
premises: The practice yields escalating fruits
A time frame of one year is given
Sovereignty is the promised result
items.inference: Within a year, he will become a sovereign ruler of the earth.
uncertainties: Continuation of the count from previous verse is implied
items.plain_english: Within a year, he will become a sovereign of the whole earth.

items.question: What result and ritual procedure are being summarized in this statement?
premises: The practice can yield wealth
Circle worship is the governing rite
A specific rule is being identified
items.inference: There may be attainment of wealth; this is the rule for circle worship.
uncertainties: The verse may bridge two clauses with compressed syntax
items.plain_english: There may be attainment of wealth; this is the rule for circle worship.

items.question: Who gains merit by giving to the intoxicated within the ritual circle?
premises: Intoxicated participants are present in the circle
Giving or service occurs in that context
Such acts generate merit
items.inference: He who gives to one intoxicated by honey in the circle indeed becomes a sharer of merit.
uncertainties: The repeated 'cakre vā cakre vā' may emphasize the setting or indicate alternatives
items.plain_english: Whether in the circle or in the circle, he who gives to one intoxicated by honey indeed shares in merit.

items.question: When does the previously described ritual action become fruitless?
premises: The ritual action has a valid period
Delay beyond that period is possible
Timeliness affects efficacy
items.inference: It is declared fruitless if performed after a month.
uncertainties: The subject is implicit, likely the offering or rite mentioned before
items.plain_english: But it is declared fruitless after a month.

items.question: How should satisfaction be offered when preceded by circle worship?
premises: Circle worship precedes the offering
Satisfaction of recipients is required
Measured substances are to be used
items.inference: One should satisfy them with balanced substances, preceded by circle worship.
uncertainties: Exact meaning of 'tuladravyaiḥ' as weighed or equivalent substances is interpretive
items.plain_english: One should satisfy them with measured offerings, preceded by circle worship.

items.question: What worship is prescribed to pacify the fault arising from the ritual lapse?
premises: A fault has arisen from prior lapse
Pacification of that fault is needed
The yoginīs are the objects of remedial worship
items.inference: O goddess, one should worship the multitude of yoginīs for the pacification of that fault.
items.plain_english: O goddess, one should worship the host of yoginīs to pacify that fault.

items.question: On which lunar occasion should the annual rite be performed?
premises: An annual rite is prescribed
Timing is specified by lunar calendar
The first day of a fortnight is chosen
items.inference: The annual rite should be performed on the first day of the fortnight.
uncertainties: The object of the rite is supplied by following verses
items.plain_english: On the first day of the fortnight, perform the annual rite.

items.question: What qualities must the girl chosen for the annual rite possess?
premises: A girl is selected for the rite
Specific age and physical qualities are required
Freedom from defect is mandated
items.inference: She should be nine years old, beautiful, and free from bodily defects.
items.plain_english: She should be nine years old, beautiful, and free from defects.

items.question: How are the nine forms of the goddess identified in this ritual enumeration?
premises: The rite involves nine forms
Gaurī and Durgā are among them
Tradition proclaims these forms
items.inference: Gaurī, Durgā, and others are proclaimed as the nine forms.
uncertainties: Only two names are listed in this verse; the full set of nine is implied by context
items.plain_english: Gaurī, Durgā, and the rest are proclaimed as the nine.

items.question: How should the selected girl be prepared and brought to the place of worship?
premises: The selected girl must be ritually purified
Oil massage and bathing accomplish purification
She must be brought to the worship place
items.inference: One should bring her, purified by oil massage and bath, to the place of worship.
items.plain_english: One should bring her, purified by oil massage and bath, to the place of worship.

items.question: With what ritual offerings should the worship of the selected girl be performed?
premises: Worship requires material offerings
Fragrance, flowers, rice, incense, and lamps are standard items
Special lamps of the lineage are included
items.inference: She should be worshipped with fragrance, flowers, unbroken rice, incense, lamps, and lineage lamps.
uncertainties: 'kuladīpakaiḥ' may refer to special lamps or metaphorically to lineage illuminators; ritual object sense preferred
items.plain_english: Worship her with fragrances, flowers, unbroken rice, incense, lamps, and lamps of the lineage.
